evaluator: Blind Stagebench Phase 2 evaluator: rebuilt the sealed artifact from source (bundle hash index-DE4a6YoS.js, identical to artifact/dist/), served it on an exclusively-owned 127.0.0.1:5403, and measured rendered audio in headless Chromium by patching AudioNode.prototype.connect to tap a ScriptProcessor off the AudioContext destination (RMS, peak, clipped-sample count, stereo side-RMS, 8192-pt FFT centroid and 6-band energy, 50 ms RMS envelope). Every effect and piano control was A/B'd on real signal rather than read from source.
summary: Architecturally this is a real Phase 2 build: one AudioContext, two per-layer buses each with the full spec-ordered chain (Mod1-Mod2-Delay-Amp/EQ-Comp-Reverb-Rotary), layer levels, master gain and limiter into one destination. Delay, Amp/EQ, Compressor, Reverb, Rotary, all-effects bypass, Master Level, layer faders, KB Touch, Dyn Comp, Unison and Soft Release all measurably move rendered audio. But the phase's headline gate fails outright: every bundled Grand/Upright/Electric WAV has a corrupt fmt chunk (audioFormat 257, channels 0) from a byte-offset bug in the generator, so decodeAudioData throws EncodingError and the app runs permanently in synthetic fallback -- honestly labelled, but no sample set ever plays. Mod 1 sums all six type paths in parallel off one LFO gain: Wah and A-Wah peak at 2.44 with 23-25% of samples clipped. Amp types Twin/JC/Small/LP24/HP24 and the delay filter modes have no panel control at all, and the Reverb Time knob touches nothing in the graph. Worst of all, the candidate's own audio tests never render audio -- measureEnergy falls back to arithmetic keyed on type.length, so 'amp types are audibly distinct' passes on string length.

evidence: All six types select and play. Measured spectral centroid of a C4 (MIDI 60) strike through the real destination tap: Grand 563 Hz, Upright 739 Hz, Electric 568 Hz, Clav 1778 Hz, Digital 450 Hz, Misc 773 Hz, with distinct 6-band energy profiles (Grand [0, .854, .146, .0008, 0, 0] vs Clav [.021, .485, .309, .173, .012, .0002]). They are more than one voice relabelled.

But no sample set ever plays. In the running build the instrument reports data-audio-status="fallback" with the visible message "Sample assets failed (grand,upright,electric) - labeled synthetic fallback active". A direct in-page check confirmed the cause: fetch('./samples/grand/r60_v1.wav') returns 200 (39734 bytes) and ctx.decodeAudioData rejects with EncodingError.

Root cause is a header bug in artifact/scripts/generate-samples.mjs:30 -- buf.writeUInt16LE(1, 21) writes numChannels at byte 21 instead of 22, leaving audioFormat=257 and numChannels=0. Verified on the sealed asset: `python3 struct.unpack_from('<H', d, 20)` = 257, offset 22 = 0; ffprobe reports codec_name=unknown, channels=0; Python's wave module raises "unknown format: 257". All 54 bundled WAVs share the identical header.

Consequence: every type, including Grand/Upright/Electric, is produced by the same 5-partial additive recipe in src/audio/sample-library.ts:67 (synthesizeBuffer). Grand vs Electric differ only in the 1.2-3 kHz band (0.00083 vs 0.01425) and by 5 Hz of centroid -- a knowledgeable player would not hear a grand against a Rhodes.

Phase 2 hard gate 1 ('Grand, Upright, and Electric are bundled recorded sample sets that are audibly distinct, work offline') is not met, though IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json is honest that the assets are offline-baked rather than recorded.

Five of seven units behave like their namesake on measured signal. Delay: 50 ms-block envelope tail (blocks 10+) 0.0895 at feedback 0 vs 0.8162 at feedback 1, with discrete repeats visible in the envelope. Amp/EQ: centroid 471 Hz at bass-max/treble-min vs 1169 Hz at bass-min/treble-max; drive 0 to 1 raises RMS 0.124 to 0.209 and quadruples the 1.2-3 kHz band (0.0011 to 0.0041). Compressor: hard/soft strike RMS ratio 3.62 with the unit off, 1.33 with amount at max -- genuine dynamic-range narrowing. Reverb: six types, tail energy Booth 0.0008 < Room 0.0032 < Spring 0.0186 < Stage 0.0425 < Hall 0.0465 < Cathedral 0.1232, matching the spec's ordering. Rotary via To Rotary: RMS +210%, centroid +316 Hz. All-effects bypass: reverb tail 0.0939 to 0.0034.

Mod 1 is broken. src/audio/effects-chain.ts:208-223 wires pan, tremolo, ring, wah and pump all in parallel into one `wet` bus, and a single lfoGain (line 220-223) feeds pan.pan, tremolo.gain, wah.frequency AND pump.gain simultaneously. Because line 516 sets lfoDepth to 400+amount*2000 for Wah, that same 2400-unit modulation lands on tremolo.gain and pump.gain. Measured at amount=1: Tremolo RMS 0.207 peak 1.21, but A-Wah RMS 0.825 peak 2.41 with 24.5% of samples clipped at full scale, and Wah RMS 0.807 peak 2.44 with 23.0% clipped. Two of six Mod 1 types produce gross clipping distortion, not a wah.

The parallel summing also destroys type isolation: A-Pan's stereo side-RMS is 0.0591, barely above Pump's 0.0539 and Tremolo's 0.0337, because the un-panned tremolo/wah/pump copies dilute the panner. Ring Mod measures side-RMS exactly 0 and is amplitude modulation with a carrier offset (ring.gain.value is ramped to `amount` at line 522), not true ring modulation.

Mod 2 is measurably distinct per type (centroids Chorus 453, Flanger 511, Phaser 570, Vibe 629, Ensemble 578, Spin 606 Hz) but strictly mono: stereo side-RMS is 0.000000 for all six. delayL and delayR both sum into one mono `wet` node (effects-chain.ts:267-268), so Chorus, Ensemble and Vibe -- widening effects by definition -- add no width, and Phaser is a delay comb rather than an all-pass network.

A majority of the spec's selectable types are unreachable from the panel. A DOM audit of the running build found no control for fx-amp-type, fx-delay-filter, fx-delay-tap, fx-comp-fast, fx-reverb-bright, fx-rotary-speed or fx-rotary-drive. AMP_TYPES and DELAY_FILTERS are imported into src/state/control-bindings.ts only to be discarded at lines 454-455 (`void AMP_TYPES`, `void DELAY_FILTERS`), so Twin, JC, Small, LP24 Filter and HP24 Filter are dead code -- only 'EQ only' and 'To Rotary' can ever be selected.

The Reverb Time knob is a no-op. `fx-reverb-time` writes chain.reverb.time (control-bindings.ts:186-191), but grep shows effects-chain.ts never reads `.time`; the only reader is the test proxy at piano-engine.ts:933. Measured tail with time at 0 vs 1: 0.0745 vs 0.0687 -- within the run-to-run noise of the randomly regenerated impulse.

One AudioContext only: my destination tap instantiated exactly one capture chain across the whole session (window.__capCtx, sampleRate 48000, state 'running'), and the graph builder in src/audio/piano-engine.ts:218-258 creates a single ctx with layerBusA/layerBusB, chainA/chainB, one shared rotary, layerLevelA/B, master gain and a DynamicsCompressor limiter (threshold -3 dB, ratio 12) into ctx.destination.

Chain order matches the spec's requiredOrder exactly: effects-chain.ts:481-489 wires input to Mod1 to Mod2 to Delay to AmpEq to Compressor to Reverb to (toRotary | directOut), and piano-engine.ts:239-252 continues reverb/rotary to layerLevel to master to limiter to destination. Reverb precedes Rotary as required.

Gain staging measured sane and monotonic. Master Level: RMS 0.140927 at 1.0, 0.069233 at 0.5, 0.000001 at 0.0 (peak 0.668 / 0.324 / 0.00001) -- linear and silent at zero. Piano Layer A fader: RMS 0.1232 at max, 0.0 at min, 0.1172 back at max. All-effects bypass measured on signal (tail 0.0939 to 0.0034).

No clipping under polyphonic load: 40 simultaneous notes (MIDI 40-79) at max strike velocity with Amp Sim + drive at max and reverb engaged measured peak 0.409, 0 clipped samples, RMS 0.094, and produced zero console errors. A 24-note run measured peak 0.891, 0 clipped.

Against that, gain staging fails inside Mod 1: the fanned-out LFO drives peak to 2.44 with 23-25% of samples at or beyond full scale, i.e. the master limiter does not protect the destination for two supported control settings (recorded separately as a major issue).

Two-layer behavior reaches the graph. Enabling Piano Layer B and shifting it +2 octaves changed a C4 strike from RMS 0.1648 / centroid 675 Hz (A alone) to RMS 0.2031 / centroid 1319 Hz (A+B), so B is a genuinely separate voice on its own bus with its own octave shift, not a level trick. Layer A's fader measured 0.1232 at max and exactly 0.0 at min.

Four detailed piano controls measurably reach the audio graph. KB Touch at the same pointer strike position: Heavy RMS 0.03449 / peak 0.179 vs Light RMS 0.08327 / peak 0.394 (2.4x). Dyn Comp on a soft strike: Off RMS 0.03433 vs level 3 RMS 0.09106 (2.65x, correct direction -- softer strokes raised). Unison across Off/1/2/3: RMS 0.1315, 0.1706, 0.1982, 0.2497 with centroid falling 548 to 430 Hz as detuning widens. Soft Release: envelope tail (blocks 6+) 0.1628 off vs 0.2214 on, a 36% longer release.

String Res does not measurably change rendered audio. Holding MIDI 48 and striking MIDI 60 so that held.size > 0 satisfies the guard at piano-engine.ts:506, the toggle moved centroid 318 Hz to 318 Hz and RMS 0.075354 to 0.075358 -- a 0.005% difference, i.e. nothing. The piano spec's acceptance clause requires String Res to measurably change rendered audio.

Timbre is inaudible on the default instrument. On Grand across Off/Soft/Mid/Bright the centroid measured 560, 454, 457, 523 Hz -- non-monotonic noise -- because timbreFilterHz (piano-engine.ts:68) is a lowpass at 1800-12000 Hz while the fallback Grand voice has essentially no energy above 3 kHz (band 4 = 0.000). On the HF-rich Clav it does work and is monotonic in cutoff (1054 Hz at Soft, 1497 at Mid, 1765 at Off, 1900/1983 at Bright/Dyno).

Dyno 1 and Dyno 2 are not distinguishable: both map to 9000 Hz with Q 2 at piano-engine.ts:71 and 464, so the two tine-preamp emulations the spec calls for are the same setting. The Reverb Time knob moves and reports a value but reaches nothing in the graph.

Failure degrades visibly, not silently -- the strongest part of this artifact. When decodeAudioData rejects all 54 sample files the engine sets status 'fallback' and the running build renders a live status bar reading "Audio: fallback" plus "Sample assets failed (grand,upright,electric) - labeled synthetic fallback active", and stays fully playable. Web MIDI without permission surfaced as data-midi-state="denied" on the instrument element rather than failing quietly.

Stable under stress: a full interaction pass (six piano-type changes, ~30 effect toggles and knob sweeps, a 24-note chord and a 40-note chord, ~120 pointer note events) produced 0 console errors and 0 failed network requests, captured via Playwright console and requestfailed listeners.

Pointer velocity is real and continuous: striking the same key near its top measured RMS 0.05677 / peak 0.2819, near its bottom RMS 0.20860 / peak 0.9037 -- a 3.7x velocity range from strike position.

Voice lifecycle survives load: 40 simultaneous notes released cleanly with peak 0.409 and 0 clipped samples; allNotesOff is wired to window blur, MIDI disconnect and unmount (src/components/Instrument.tsx:113, 118-131) and the Panic button calls engine.allNotesOff (control-bindings.ts:198).

One silent no-op against it: fx-reverb-time is classified functional by isFunctionalControl (control-bindings.ts:31-34, 'fx-' prefix), moves, and reports aria-valuenow, yet changes nothing audible -- a control that reports success it does not deliver.

Present and exercised: six selectable piano types, two layers with enable/focus/level/octave, KB Touch, Dyn Comp, Unison, Soft Release, sustain (UI toggle, keyboard, MIDI CC64), the labeled fallback, all six effect units plus a shared rotary in the documented order, per-unit on/bypass, all-effects bypass, focus/group/global state, a functional Master Level knob and a working Panic. tests/feature-matrix.json declares all 20 required feature IDs and inputs/verification.json records coveredFeatures 20 / requiredFeatures 20.

Missing required elements measured against the specs: recorded Grand/Upright/Electric sample sets never load (EncodingError on every file); String Res has no measurable audio effect; Amp/EQ types Twin, JC, Small, LP24 Filter and HP24 Filter plus the Delay feedback filter modes Off/LP/HP/BP have no panel control and so cannot be selected at all; Compressor Fast, Reverb Bright/Dark and Rotary Slow/Fast + Drive likewise have no control (DOM audit of the running build found none of fx-amp-type, fx-delay-filter, fx-comp-fast, fx-reverb-bright, fx-rotary-speed, fx-rotary-drive).

The coverage that is claimed is not verified by the tests that claim it. Every effects test calls PianoEngine.measureEnergy, which is a parallel reimplementation, not the real graph. I instrumented the candidate's own test environment: `typeof OfflineAudioContext` is "undefined" and `typeof AudioContext` is "undefined" under jsdom, so measureEnergy always takes the arithmetic branch at piano-engine.ts:890-937. Measured in that environment, ampEq type 'Twin' yields 0.5803481249999999 and 'JC' yields 0.5342887499999999 -- they differ only because line 925 computes `chain.ampEq.type.length * 0.05` and 'Twin' has 4 characters against 'JC''s 2. The test named 'Amp types are audibly distinct' therefore passes on string length while the five amp types it names are unreachable dead code.

Same pattern elsewhere: mod1/mod2/reverb 'types are distinct' tests key off `type.charCodeAt(0)` hashes (lines 913, 917, 932); typeSignature returns a hardcoded lookup table {Grand:[1,0.4,0.2,base], Upright:[1,0.55,0.3,base*1.05], ...} when OfflineAudioContext is absent (piano-engine.ts:952-960); and piano-instrument-library.test.ts asserts getStatus()==='ready' only because it passes useInlineSamples:true, which bypasses fetch and decode entirely -- which is exactly why no test caught that all 54 shipped WAVs are undecodable.

IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md ticks all five Phase 2 hard gates as done, including 'Grand, Upright, and Electric are bundled recorded sample sets that are audibly distinct, work offline' and 'Every functional piano and effect control measurably changes rendered audio'; measurement on the running build contradicts both.

issues.title: All 54 bundled sample WAVs are undecodable; the sample-playback path never runs
issues.detail: scripts/generate-samples.mjs:30 writes numChannels with buf.writeUInt16LE(1, 21) instead of offset 22, clobbering the audioFormat field. Every shipped file therefore has audioFormat=257 and numChannels=0. Verified independently three ways on artifact/public/samples/grand/r60_v1.wav: Chrome decodeAudioData rejects with EncodingError in the running build, ffprobe reports codec_name=unknown / channels=0, and Python's wave module raises "unknown format: 257". The app consequently reports data-audio-status="fallback" on every load and synthesises all six piano types, so Phase 2's first hard gate is unmet even though the files, manifests and multi-root/multi-velocity picker logic are all present and correct.

issues.title: No audio test renders audio: measureEnergy degrades to a string-hash formula under jsdom
issues.detail: PianoEngine.measureEnergy builds a separate offline proxy graph rather than the real chain, and when OfflineAudioContext is unavailable it falls back to arithmetic over state (piano-engine.ts:890-937). I confirmed by instrumenting the candidate's own suite that both OfflineAudioContext and AudioContext are undefined under its jsdom environment, so the arithmetic branch always runs: amp type 'Twin' returns 0.5803481249999999 and 'JC' returns 0.5342887499999999 purely because of `type.length * 0.05`. typeSignature similarly returns a hardcoded per-type array. All six tests in tests/effects-processing.test.ts, plus the distinctness tests in tests/piano-instrument-library.test.ts, assert on these proxies. The suite reports 66/66 passing while shipping two clipping Mod 1 types, five unreachable amp types, a dead Reverb Time knob and a completely broken sample library.

issues.title: Mod 1 Wah and A-Wah clip 23-25% of output samples
issues.detail: effects-chain.ts:220-223 connects one lfoGain node to pan.pan, tremolo.gain, wah.frequency and pump.gain at once, and line 516 sets that gain to 400+amount*2000 for the Wah types. The filter-sweep depth therefore also lands on two gain parameters. Measured at Mod 1 amount = 1, rate = 0.5, on a single C4: A-Wah RMS 0.8248 / peak 2.4081 / 24.5% of samples clipped, Wah RMS 0.8069 / peak 2.4417 / 23.0% clipped, against Tremolo RMS 0.2072 / peak 1.2119 / 0.2% clipped. Two of six Mod 1 types are unusable and the master limiter does not contain them.

issues.title: Mod 1 type paths sum in parallel, so no type is isolated
issues.detail: effects-chain.ts:208-218 permanently connects the input to pan, tremolo, ring, wah and pump, all of which sum into a single wet gain. Selecting a type only changes LFO depth constants; the other four paths keep passing signal. Measured stereo side-RMS: A-Pan 0.0591 against Pump 0.0539 and Tremolo 0.0337 -- the dedicated panner is barely wider than effects that should be mono. Ring Mod measures side-RMS 0.000000 and is amplitude modulation with a carrier offset (ring.gain ramped to `amount` at line 522), not ring modulation. A-Wah differs from Wah only by two depth constants and has no envelope follower despite the spec calling for one.

issues.title: Amp/EQ types and Delay feedback filter modes cannot be selected at all
issues.detail: The effects spec requires every listed type to be selectable and audibly distinct within its unit. src/model/hardware.ts ships no fx-amp-type or fx-delay-filter control, and src/state/control-bindings.ts imports AMP_TYPES and DELAY_FILTERS only to discard them at lines 454-455 (`void AMP_TYPES`, `void DELAY_FILTERS`). A DOM audit of the running build confirmed no such elements exist. Twin, JC, Small, LP24 Filter and HP24 Filter are implemented in applyAmpEq but reachable only through code; from the panel the amp unit can be 'EQ only' or, via the To Rotary button, 'To Rotary'. The delay's per-repeat filter, tap tempo, master-clock sync and ping-pong are likewise absent, as are Compressor Fast, Reverb Bright/Dark and Rotary Slow/Fast + Drive.

issues.title: String Res produces no measurable change in rendered audio
issues.detail: The piano spec's acceptance list requires String Res to measurably change rendered audio. With MIDI 48 held so that the held.size > 0 guard at piano-engine.ts:506 is satisfied and MIDI 60 struck, toggling the control moved centroid from 318 Hz to 318 Hz and RMS from 0.075354 to 0.075358 -- 0.005%, indistinguishable from noise. addStringRes adds three sines at gain 0.03*vel against a main voice peaking near 0.5, roughly -30 dB, and the resonance is attached to the striking voice's own amp rather than to the sympathetically-ringing held notes.

issues.title: Reverb Time knob is a functional-looking control with no audio effect
issues.detail: fx-reverb-time is treated as functional by isFunctionalControl (control-bindings.ts:31-34) and writes chain.reverb.time (lines 186-191), but applyReverb in effects-chain.ts never reads `.time`; the property's only reader in the whole codebase is the arithmetic test proxy at piano-engine.ts:933. Measured reverb tail energy with the knob at 0 vs 1: 0.0745 vs 0.0687, inside the run-to-run variance introduced by regenerating a random impulse on every apply. The knob moves and reports aria-valuenow while delivering nothing, which is the failure mode the honesty contract exists to prevent.

issues.title: Mod 2 is entirely mono; no widening effect widens
issues.detail: effects-chain.ts:267-268 sums delayL and delayR into one mono wet node. Measured stereo side-RMS at amount = 1 is exactly 0.000000 for all six types (Chorus, Flanger, Phaser, Vibe, Ensemble, Spin). Chorus, Vibe and Ensemble are defined by stereo spread, and Ensemble specifically calls for three cross-connected modulated delay lines; here all six are one mono comb filter differentiated only by depth and feedback constants, and Phaser uses that comb rather than an all-pass network.

issues.title: Timbre inaudible on acoustic types; Dyno 1 and Dyno 2 are identical
issues.detail: timbreFilterHz (piano-engine.ts:68-75) implements all Timbre settings as a single lowpass cutoff. On the default Grand the fallback voice carries no energy above 3 kHz, so Off/Soft/Mid/Bright measured centroids of 560, 454, 457 and 523 Hz -- non-monotonic and within noise. On Clav it works and tracks cutoff monotonically (1054 / 1497 / 1765 / 1900 Hz). Separately, 'Dyno 1' and 'Dyno 2' both return 9000 Hz with Q 2 (lines 71 and 464), so the two tine-preamp emulations the spec distinguishes are the same setting, and Mid is a wider lowpass rather than the midrange presence lift the manual describes.

issues.title: pnpm build fails on a clean lockfile install (missing @types/node)
issues.detail: Reproduced on a fresh rsync of artifact/ with `pnpm install` from the sealed pnpm-lock.yaml under Node 24.19.0 / pnpm 11.7.0: `pnpm build` (tsc --noEmit && vite build) exits 2 with four TS2591 errors in tests/regression-phase1.test.tsx lines 9, 10, 37 and 58 -- 'node:fs', 'node:path' and 'process' are used in a tsconfig-included file while @types/node is absent from package.json. The installed dependency trees are byte-identical between artifact/node_modules and my copy, and the source files diff clean, so the failure is reproducible rather than a copy artifact. `vite build` alone succeeds and reproduces the sealed bundle exactly (index-DE4a6YoS.js). inputs/verification.json records this check as passing at seal time, so I have not treated it as a gate failure, only as a portability defect.

issues.title: IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md ticks hard gates that measurement contradicts
issues.detail: The plan's checklist marks all five Phase 2 hard gates complete, including 'Grand, Upright, and Electric are bundled recorded sample sets that are audibly distinct, work offline, and have complete redistributable provenance' and 'Every functional piano and effect control measurably changes rendered audio and agrees with its panel feedback'. The build never decodes a sample and at least two functional controls (Reverb Time, String Res) change nothing audible. IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json itself is honest -- it states plainly that the assets are offline-baked rather than mic recordings -- so the inaccuracy is confined to the plan's self-assessment and to the tests that were meant to substantiate it.
